text: Sometimes it isn't a reward at all. It's a rule. Same trap.
In November 1989, Mexico City tried to clean up its air with a simple rule: one weekday a week, your car stays home — decided by the last digit of your license plate.
The idea: take about one car in five off the road every weekday.
But people still had to get to work. So some families bought a second car — with a different last digit. Often an older, cheaper one that polluted more.
Economist Lucas Davis later studied years of readings from the city's air monitors. He found no evidence the rule made the air any cleaner — and evidence that it put more cars on the road.
The city wanted cleaner air. It targeted license plates. So people bought license plates — with a car attached.
